column1: # Files malware leaves on disk. One line each, tab separated. After editing, run: bash tools/gen.sh
#   os        all, mac, linux or win (win is Git Bash and gird-check.ps1)
#   kind      wiper    a file of gh-token-monitor (its path must name it), the wiper that runs a destructive command when a
#                      stolen GitHub token is revoked. Section 5 tells people to stop it first.
#             startup  a file that starts malware at login; the note is shown under it
#             site     a file in any Python environment's site-packages: a Python incident's hit
#             temp     an entry in /tmp, TMPDIR or %TEMP%: a Python incident's hit. May end in *
#   owner     yes: counts only if this person owns it (for files in the shared /tmp). no otherwise
#   path      wiper and startup: a file or folder, with the path tokens data/sessions.tsv uses, an
#             absolute path, or {PROGRAMDATA} (Windows' ProgramData). site and temp: a file name
#   note      startup: what the file does, as shown. - for the other kinds
# gh-token-monitor: Wiz (TanStack wave) and SANS (keyv wave). Mastra: Socket. LiteLLM and mistralai: their advisories.
